title: Why using rocks for carbon removal could eventually reduce crop growth
gist: Two CarbonPlan preprints find that soil alkalization from heavy crushed-rock application would hurt crop yields, capping enhanced rock weathering's realistic potential near 600 million tons of CO2 per year versus model estimates of 3-8 billion. This lands as Google, Frontier and others have committed about $670 million to ERW amid ongoing disputes over measurement and permanence.
